title: Use schema-correct ChatMessage identifiers in action authority queries
description:
As a procedure operator, I want blocking and advisory human-action readers to use schema-correct GraphQL variable types, so that persisted responses can be validated and claimed against the deployed API.

Out of scope: schema, model, index, association, storage, IAM, or function changes.

Scenario: Blocking action response lookup
  Given an existing pending ChatMessage action
  When the runtime reads the parent and child responses through the deployed GraphQL schema
  Then the query uses an ID variable for getChatMessage and a String variable for the parent-message index
  And the same opaque identifier is supplied to both variables

Scenario: Advisory action response lookup
  Given an existing advisory ChatMessage action
  When the reconciler reads the parent and child responses
  Then the query is schema-valid and preserves the same opaque identifier

Scenario: Missing authority
  Given the ChatMessage authority dependency is unavailable
  When the runtime evaluates an action
  Then it fails closed without accepting a response.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Sandbox reproduction confirmed before any optimizer launch: deployed GraphQL rejected the shared String variable at getChatMessage, which requires ID. Adding schema-contract coverage for separate ID and parent-index variables before the minimal reader fix.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: The minimal query fix now has green focused and full CI evidence on Python 3.11 and 3.12. Both readers supply the same opaque identifier through schema-correct ID and String variables, and missing authority remains fail-closed. Final sandbox response-claim acceptance is in progress.
